data.title: A warm visual style and a favicon for "Split the bill"

events.goal: Make the "Split the bill" interface neat, warm and friendly
requirements: Work fully on your own and take the task through the process: statement, code, review, checks, commit
I approve the statement in advance; on the analyst's questions choose the simpler and cleaner option and write the decision into the statement
On the third rework don't stop: decide yourself, simplify what doesn't work and note it in the report
Don't bypass or disable checks, commit in small commits and push, don't rewrite git history
Don't take UI frameworks or new dependencies: only TypeScript, DOM and CSS, system fonts, icons as inline SVG, not emoji
Don't change the domain logic or behaviour, only the look, the markup and the captions
Move the DOM tests that looked for a button by the text "Remove" to a search by role and accessible name

Define tokens as CSS variables in one place: the light theme follows my palette with the accent #0E7C66 and "gives" #C2410C, the dark one follows prefers-color-scheme with contrast no lower than WCAG AA
Keep radii of 12 px on cards and 10 px on fields and buttons, a barely visible shadow, spacing on the 4/8/12/16/24/32 scale
Typography: system-ui, page heading 28 px, section headings 20 px, text 16 px, captions 14 px; amounts are tabular-nums and right-aligned
In the header give the title, the subtitle "Who owes whom and how much, without spreadsheets or arguments" and an overview: participants, expenses, total spent
The primary button is filled with the accent, the secondary one is outlined, removal is a cross icon with a caption for screen readers; focus is visible, touch targets are at least 44 px
Show participants as chips with an avatar: the first letter of the name on one of 8 soft colors, the color is derived stably from the name
Put the name field and the "Add" button on one line
Show expenses as a row with the payer's avatar, the name, a grey caption "for everyone" or "for: Ann, Ben" and the amount on the right; "For whom" is toggle chips on top of real checkboxes
Make the summary the main block: each transfer is an "avatar → avatar" card with a large amount, with a line about the number of transfers above them
Hide "How it is calculated" in an expandable block with a table: participant, paid, share, balance; tell "receives" and "gives" apart by color, sign and word
Instead of empty cards give friendly hints
On a phone one column from 360 px, from 900 px two: participants and expenses on the left, a sticky column with the summary and "Share" on the right
Add 150 ms transitions to buttons and chips and turn them off under prefers-reduced-motion
Record the style in AGENTS.md as an "Interface style" section
Take Playwright screenshots at 360×800, 768×1024 and 1280×800, in the light and dark theme, empty and filled, look at them and fix everything that is off
Replace docs/screenshot.png with a 390×844 screenshot, add docs/screenshot-desktop.png at 1280×800 and update the README
When you finish, publish the session recording: check the draft and the tables yourself against the rules and publish without me
Commit the recording, push, open a PR into main and merge it
In the final report describe the changes to the look with links to the screenshots, the decisions made without me, and what I need to do by hand

events.line: Got it, I'll study the code and write the statement
events.text:
Write the statement for a task of the split-bill project: study the code and write the statement. It needs a step-by-step plan split into small coherent commits, a list of files, verifiable done criteria and risks. The human approved the statement in advance and is unavailable. If questions come up, choose the simpler and cleaner option and write the decision straight into the statement as "Decision: …". Leave no questions for the human.

The human's task: a visual style for "Split the bill". The interface is built from standard browser elements and looks raw: grey system buttons, no accent color, the "Remove" buttons stand out the most, the main thing (who transfers to whom) is hidden at the bottom as a plain list, the amounts are not aligned. The app needs to become neat and pleasant, like a good mobile money app, but warmer and friendlier.

Constraints: no UI frameworks or new dependencies, only TypeScript, DOM and CSS; system fonts, icons as inline SVG, not emoji; the domain logic and behaviour do not change; the existing tests stay green, and where they looked for a button by the text "Remove", they move to a search by role and accessible name; checks are not bypassed.

Style: tokens as CSS variables in one place, a light theme by the given palette and a dark one with contrast no lower than WCAG AA; radii, a barely visible shadow, a spacing scale and typography; a header with a subtitle and an overview; primary and secondary buttons and a cross remove button with a caption for screen readers, visible focus, touch targets of at least 44 px; participants as chips with an avatar whose color is derived stably from the name; expenses as a row with the payer's avatar; the summary as the main block with transfer cards and an expandable "How it is calculated" block; friendly empty states; one column on a phone and two from 900 px with a sticky right column; 150 ms transitions turned off under reduced-motion; a description of the style in an "Interface style" section of AGENTS.md.

Checking the look is mandatory: Playwright screenshots at three sizes, in the light and dark theme, empty and filled. Don't download browsers, keep the script outside the repository. Look at the shots, fix what is off, replace the screenshot in docs, add a desktop one and update the README.

In the statement, specify how to get the filled state for the screenshots through a link with a bill, which captions and tests change, how the avatar color is computed by a deterministic function of the name, and how to check the contrast of the dark theme: calculate and record the pairs with their ratios. The answer is the whole statement.

events.line: Here it is. The statement is ready: nine steps
events.text:
The statement is ready. Goal: "Split the bill" gets a neat, warm look with style tokens, light and dark themes, chips with avatars, transfer cards, a "How it is calculated" table and two columns on a wide screen. The calculation logic and behaviour do not change.

The task was given as text in the session, so commits carry no issue reference. The logic of the bill, the calculation and the links is not touched, and the generated file with the agent's rules is not edited.

The main decisions made instead of the human where the task left a choice. The captions of the remove buttons stay as they are: arbitrary names cannot be declined without a library, and a short caption would make expenses of one payer indistinguishable. Buttons in tests are found by a helper of their own by role and accessible name, without new libraries. The avatar color is derived from the name by a deterministic function onto eight tones, and the colors themselves live only in CSS. There is one avatar palette for both themes, and the text on it is always dark. Tokens are added for the field border, the text on the accent, the error, the warning and the shadow. The "How it is calculated" block is built with details and summary and is closed by default. The "Balance" column of the table shows a word and a signed amount, and "receives" and "gives" are also told apart by color. "For whom" is chosen with chips on top of real checkboxes. The right column from 900 px is sticky, with a height limit and scrolling inside.

The statement calculates the contrast pairs for the light and dark themes and for all eight avatar colors: text pairs are no lower than 4.5, non-text ones no lower than 3.

A plan of nine commits: finding buttons by role in tests; tokens, themes and buttons; icons and avatars; the header with the overview; participants and expenses; the summary and the table; two columns; the "Interface style" section in AGENTS.md; new screenshots and README. After each commit the checks are green.

Checking the look: a build, a preview and a Playwright script in a temporary directory. It needs shots at three sizes in two themes, the empty and the filled state (the README example through a link with a bill) and a stress bill with a long name. On each shot the absence of horizontal overflow is checked, then the shots are looked at by eye.

Done criteria: checks green after each commit, the logic untouched, colors only in the token blocks, the needed media queries in place, buttons and chips no smaller than 44 px, the overview and the summary match the README example, empty states are visible, the layout works at all widths, the section in AGENTS.md exists, the screenshots have the right size.

Tests: rewrite the helpers in the interface tests, add tests of the header, the remove buttons, the same avatar tone for a person everywhere, empty states, the line about the number of transfers and the summary classes, and a separate test of the avatar functions.

Risks: a sticky column taller than the screen, four table columns at 360 px, test selectors after the split into columns, counting the explanations in the summary, support for :has() and keeping the number of avatar tones in sync between the code and the CSS.

events.line: Got it, I'm following the plan step by step
events.text:
Do the task of the split-bill project by the approved statement. Read it in full first and follow it: decisions, commit plan, checking the look, done criteria, tests. The project's rules are in its rule files.

Go through the plan from the first step to the ninth. After each step format the code, get the checks green and make a local commit in the Conventional Commits format with the message from the plan and the closing authorship lines. Don't push or rewrite history. If a fix after checking the look touches a step already committed, make a separate fix(ui) commit.

Check the look without fail and honestly: keep the Playwright script outside the repository, use the installed Chromium as it is, download nothing and add nothing to package.json. Open the shots and look at them by eye: three widths, two themes, the empty and the filled state, plus the open "How it is calculated" block. Fix everything that is off: overflow, truncated captions, misaligned amounts, weak contrast, ugly spacing. Repeat until the look is neat, like a good mobile money app, but warm. Then take the final screenshots for docs.

Don't change the domain logic, the dependencies or the file with the agent's rules. Don't bypass or disable checks. If you had to deviate from the plan, write it in the report.

The report needs: the list of commits, what was done for each done criterion and what confirms it, deviations from the plan, what you saw on the shots and what you fixed, where the final shots are, and the result of the last run of the checks.

events.line: Here it is. All 9 steps are done, checks green
events.text:
All nine steps of the plan are done, the checks are green, 313 tests pass, the working tree is clean. Nothing is pushed, I didn't rewrite history. I checked the look on Playwright shots, found and fixed a few flaws.

Ten commits are made: tests finding buttons by role, tokens and themes, icons and avatars, the header with the overview, participants and expenses, the summary with cards and the table, two columns, layout fixes after checking the look, the "Interface style" section in AGENTS.md, and new screenshots with the README. Formatting and the checks passed before each commit.

On the done criteria: the logic, the dependencies and the file with the agent's rules are untouched; colors appear only in the two token blocks; the needed media queries are in place, 150 ms transitions only when motion is allowed; icons are created by a shared helper and hidden from screen readers; buttons and chips are no smaller than 44 px; the overview for the README example reads "4 participants · 3 expenses · spent 6 650,50 ₽"; the summary shows "3 transfers are needed to settle up" and three cards with amounts on the right; "How it is calculated" expands, "receives" and "gives" differ by color, sign and word; empty states are visible; at 360 and 768 px there is one column, from 900 px two with a sticky right one, and there is no overflow on any of the thirty shots in both themes; the contrast is recalculated by a separate script and all pairs match the table in AGENTS.md; the 780×1688 mobile screenshot and the 1280×800 desktop one are in docs, and the README links to them.

Deviations from the plan: two extra shared helpers (the empty-state hint and the remove button), a chip container inside the "For whom" group, the participant name in the table as a row header, four additional size tokens, wrapping of names in the table, and one layout fix commit after checking the look.

What I saw on the shots and fixed: the overview in the header wrapped at 360 px with a dangling separator dot; the table overflowed the page by 30 px at 360 px, and words broke in the middle; empty states had extra spacing. All of it is fixed, and a stress bill with a long name doesn't break the page.

Limitations: in stress mode on a wide screen the sticky column scrolls inside itself; the favicon stayed in the old color; noticed along the way but not touched: an old comment with an emoji in the bill logic.

events.line: Got it, I'll check against the plan and the shots
events.text:
Review the changes of the split-bill project: the implementer has already committed them locally. Compare with the base commit, there is no local main branch. The task and the approved statement with the done criteria are in the plan file, read it. The decision to keep the old captions of the remove buttons was made by the lead on purpose, don't send it back for that.

Deviations from the plan according to the implementer's report: shared helpers were added for the empty-state hint and the remove button; a chip container appeared inside the "For whom" group; the first cell of a table row became a row header; size tokens were added; names in the table wrap, and "Balance" wraps onto two lines on a narrow screen; the layout fixes after checking the look are gathered in one commit.

The Playwright shots are in the temporary files directory, the final ones in docs. Look at least at a few. The lead noticed on the dark 360 px shot with the block open: the "Paid" and "Share" columns of the "How it is calculated" table almost stick together. Assess it.

Check conformance to the plan and the human's requirements: tokens only in the :root blocks, the dark theme no lower than AA, buttons, chips, the summary as the main block, empty states, the layout, motion, AGENTS.md and README. Check the project's rules: naming, one function one action, no magic values, readability, nesting, exhaustive branching, tests next to the code that check behaviour. Check accessibility: focus, hiding the decorative from screen readers, checkboxes under the chips, 44 px targets. Make sure the bill logic, the dependencies and the file with the agent's rules are unchanged.

Verdict: ACCEPTED, or SENT BACK FOR REWORK with a list of concrete remarks: where, what is wrong and how it should be.

events.line: Sending it back: table columns merge, plus small things
events.text:
SENT BACK FOR REWORK.

What I checked: the checks are green, 313 tests pass. The bill logic, the dependencies and the file with the agent's rules are untouched. Colors in the styles appear only in the two token blocks. I recalculated every contrast pair from the table in AGENTS.md from the tokens: they match to the hundredth and meet AA. Icons are created only by the shared helper and are hidden from screen readers, and so are avatars. The remove buttons are 44×44 crosses with the old captions. The "For whom" checkboxes are real, and focus is visible. Transitions are declared only when motion is allowed. From 900 px there are two columns, the right one sticky with a height limit. Empty states, the overview, the line about the number of transfers and "How it is calculated" are done by the plan. The screenshots in docs have the right size, and the README links to both. The implementer's deviations are justified.

Remarks.

First, serious. The "Paid" and "Share" columns of the "How it is calculated" table merge on a phone. Both are right-aligned, and there are only about 8 px between them, twice the spaces inside the amount itself, so "4 800,00 ₽ 1 616,84 ₽" reads as one string. Even at 1280 the gap is about 15 px, noticeably less than between the other columns. The left padding of the numeric cells needs to grow: on a narrow screen no less than a large step of the spacing scale, more on a wide one. If the stress data lacks the width, squeeze the name column on screens up to 480 px. After the fix repeat the overflow check at 360 on the README example and on the stress data in both themes and retake the shots. The screenshots in docs are not affected, the table is closed there.

Second. Sizes and values remain as literals in the styles: the maximum width of the name column in the table, the offset of the separator in the overview and the brightness on hover. This contradicts the rule the implementer wrote into AGENTS.md and the human's requirement that the rest of the CSS use tokens only. They need to become tokens, or the wording of the rule needs to be refined: the rule and the code must not diverge.

Third, minor. The class of the balance cell is chosen by substitution like outcome-kind instead of exhaustive branching as in the plan. The substitution covers all the variants and is pinned by a test, so it is acceptable, but the deviation is worth mentioning in the report.

Fourth. AGENTS.md doesn't describe the second layout breakpoint, the compact mode up to 480 px, where the margins are narrower and the table is 13 px. One line about it is needed.

Fifth, cosmetic. In the test of the summary hint the helper function is typed "string or undefined", though it always returns a string. The type needs fixing.

The rest is fine. A long 40-character name in an expense row at 360 px wraps onto five or six lines and looks somewhat heavy, but there is no overflow, and for stress data that is acceptable.

Rework after review. The statement is in the plan file, read it. You already did the task in ten commits, the branch is pushed. Previous attempt: all nine steps of the plan, checks green, 313 tests; deviations: two shared helpers, a chip container in the "For whom" group, a row header in the table, additional size tokens, wrapping of names in the table and the look fixes in one commit. The Playwright shots and scripts are still in the temporary directory, use them.

Remarks of the first review round.

First. In the "How it is calculated" table on a phone the "Paid" and "Share" columns merge: there are only 8 px between the right-aligned numbers, about 15 px at 1280. Increase the left padding of the numeric cells: on a narrow screen no less than a large step of the scale, noticeably more on a wide one. If the stress data lacks the width, squeeze the name column on screens up to 480 px. Repeat the overflow check at 360 on the README example and on the stress data in both themes, retake and look at the shots with the block open at 360, 768 and 1280.

Second. Literals remain in the styles: the maximum width of the name column, the offset of the separator in the overview and the brightness on hover. Move them into tokens with clear names, so that the rule in AGENTS.md and the code don't diverge.

Third. Don't change the substitution of the balance class by kind: the lead accepted it.

Fourth. In AGENTS.md, add a line about the compact mode up to 480 px to the layout rules: narrower margins, the table in 13 px.

Fifth. In the test of the summary hint fix the type of the helper function: it returns a string, not a string or undefined.

Rules: format and get the checks green before each commit; commits are small, in the Conventional Commits format in Russian, with the closing authorship lines; no history rewriting and no push. Don't touch the bill logic, the dependencies or the file with the agent's rules. Retake the screenshots in docs only if they visibly changed.

The report needs: the commits, what was done for each remark, the gaps between the numeric columns before and after at 360 and 1280, the result of the overflow check, where the new shots are and the result of the checks.

events.line: Here it is. All 5 remarks are fixed
events.text:
All five remarks are fixed, the checks are green. There is no overflow either on the page or inside the table. The branch is not pushed, no history rewriting.

Four commits are made: the sizes of the table, the separator and the hover moved into tokens; the numeric columns of the "How it is calculated" table spread apart; the type of the hint in the test fixed; the mobile screenshot updated after narrowing the margins.

On the remarks. First: the gap is now set by the left padding of the numeric cells, 24 px on a wide screen and 12 px on screens up to 480 px, and the right padding is removed. The name column did not need squeezing. At 360 px the table still came out 4 px wider than its container, so on screens up to 480 px the page margins are narrowed from one step of the scale to a smaller one. This is a deviation from the plan, it was not in the list of remarks. Now the table is exactly the width of the container, with no margin to spare: if the amounts get longer, it will start scrolling inside. Because of the narrower margins the mobile screenshot changed, and I updated it by retaking it; the desktop one did not change. Second: the three literals moved into tokens in the :root block and were added to the "Sizes" line in AGENTS.md. Third: I didn't touch the substitution of the balance class. Fourth: a line about the compact mode up to 480 px is added to AGENTS.md. Fifth: the type of the hint is fixed.

The gaps between the "Paid" and "Share" columns: at 360 px on the README example it was 8 px, now 12; at 1280 px on the README example it was 14.5 px, now 24; on the stress data at 1280 it was 8, now 24. The gap before the "Balance" column depends on whether its text wraps.

The overflow check: I ran the script at 360, 768 and 1280 px in both themes on five variants, empty, the README example with the block closed and open, and the stress data with the block closed and open. Everywhere the page is no wider than the window, the tables don't scroll, touch targets are no smaller than 44 px. I looked at the shots with the block open: the numbers read separately. In the "Balance" column at 360 px "receives +3 183,16 ₽" wraps onto two lines, as before. On the wide shot the sticky right column is cut at the screen height, which is not related to the fix.

events.line: Got it, I'll check whether the remarks are closed
events.text:
A repeat review of the split-bill project. The statement and the criteria are in the plan file; the rules are in the project's files. The whole task is the difference from the base commit, and the rework after the first review is the last four commits.

The remarks of the first round: the "Paid" and "Share" columns of the "How it is calculated" table merged, a noticeable gap is needed; the literals of the maximum width of the name column, the separator offset and the brightness on hover must move into tokens; the lead accepted the substitution of the balance class, don't send it back for that; AGENTS.md needs to describe the compact mode up to 480 px; the type of the hint in the test must be a string. The decision to keep the old captions of the remove buttons is also made, don't send it back for that.

According to the implementer's report: the gap between the columns is now set by tokens, 24 px on a wide screen and 12 px on screens up to 480 px, and the right padding of the cells is removed. For the table to fit at 360 px, the page margins on such screens are narrowed, which is a deviation from the plan; the table is exactly the width of the container, with no margin to spare. The mobile screenshot was retaken. The literals moved into tokens.

Check that the remarks are closed and nothing is broken, including the project's checks, colors only in the token blocks and AGENTS.md matching the code. Look at a few shots. Assess the "table with no margin" risk: is the safety net of scrolling inside the table block enough. Don't invent new requirements beyond the plan.

Verdict: ACCEPTED, or SENT BACK FOR REWORK with concrete remarks.

events.line: Accepted. The remarks are closed, passing it to checks
events.text:
ACCEPTED.

All the remarks of the first round are closed, nothing is broken.

First: the "Paid" and "Share" columns no longer merge. The gap is set by the left padding of the cells: 24 px on a wide screen and 12 px on screens up to 480 px. I measured the real gap between the texts of neighbouring numeric cells: no less than 12 px at widths from 320 to 480 px and no less than 24 px from 481 px. It is visible on the shots too.

Second: the literals moved into tokens in the :root block, each with a comment on "why". Third: as agreed, I didn't check the substitution of the balance class. Fourth: AGENTS.md has a point about the compact mode up to 480 px, and it matches the code; the new tokens are listed in the "Sizes" section. Fifth: the type of the hint in the test is now a string.

Checks: format, types, the linter, 313 tests and the build are green. Colors in the styles are found only in the two token blocks. The bill logic, the dependencies and the file with the agent's rules are unchanged, the working copy is clean. The screenshots in docs: 780×1688 and 107 KB, 1280×800 and 93 KB, the README links to both.

The "table with no margin" risk. The safety net of scrolling inside the table block is enough. I ran Playwright myself at 320, 360, 390, 480 and 481 px with three bills: the README example, amounts up to 123 456,78 ₽ and amounts up to 12 345 678,90 ₽. The page never overflowed. The README example at 360 px fits exactly, without scrolling. If the table doesn't fit, because of large amounts or a 320 px width, only the table block scrolls inside the card, and the layout doesn't break. Narrowing the page margins on screens up to 480 px is justified and described in AGENTS.md.

A small thing, not blocking: in the styles the rule of zero left padding on the first header cell of the table is now redundant and could be removed, it doesn't affect behaviour.

events.line: Got it, I'll check the done criteria
events.text:

Verdict: CHECKS PASSED, or DEFECT with specifics: the criterion, what was expected, what was obtained.

CHECKS PASSED.

I didn't edit the project's code or add tests: all criteria are confirmed by the existing tests and by observation.

The project's checks are green on the last commit: format, types, the linter, 313 tests in 11 files and the build. I ran them on each of the 14 commits from the base in a separate working copy, all passed, and I removed the copy. events.line: PR merged, CI green, the task report is ready
events.text:
CI passed, and I merged PR number 6 into main. The task went through the process: statement, code, review, checks, commit, publishing the recording.

What changed in the look. The screenshots are in the repository: a 390×844 mobile one and a 1280×800 desktop one. All colors, spacing, radii and font sizes are set by CSS variables after your palette. The dark theme turns on by prefers-color-scheme, the contrast of each pair is no lower than WCAG AA, and the table is in AGENTS.md. The header got a subtitle and a one-line overview: "4 participants · 3 expenses · spent 6 650,50 ₽". The primary buttons are filled with the green accent, "Close" is outlined, removal is a small cross with a 44×44 tap area, and focus is visible everywhere. Participants are chips with a round avatar: the first letter of the name on one of 8 soft colors, and a name always gets the same color. The name field and "Add" are on one line. An expense is a row with the payer's avatar, a grey caption "for everyone" or "for: …" and the amount on the right; "For whom" is chosen with check-mark chips on top of real checkboxes. Above the transfers is the line "3 transfers are needed to settle up", and each transfer is a card with a large amount. "How it is calculated" expands, "receives +…" and "gives −…" differ by color, sign and word. Instead of empty cards there are friendly hints with icons. On a phone there is one column, from 900 px two, the right one with the summary and "Share" sticks while scrolling, and up to 480 px there is a compact mode. Transitions are 150 ms, and there are none under reduced-motion. AGENTS.md got an "Interface style" section, and the README is updated.

The screenshots were taken at 360, 768 and 1280 px, in both themes, empty and filled, and looked through. There is no horizontal overflow on any of them. The checks are green on every commit, with 313 tests.

Decisions made without you. The captions of the crosses stayed as they were, "Remove participant Ann" and "Remove expense: Ann — 4 800,00 ₽, for everyone": arbitrary names cannot be declined without a library, and a short caption would not tell apart the expenses of one payer. For the field borders and the secondary button a darker color is introduced, because your border color on white gives a contrast of 1.28:1, and 3:1 is needed; colors for the text on the accent, the error and the warning are added. The dark theme colors were chosen on my own. Up to 480 px the table is set in a 13 px font and the page margins are narrowed, otherwise the README example did not fit in 360 px; if the amounts are larger, the table scrolls inside the card. "How it is calculated" is collapsed by default, and the explanation of the number of transfers moved inside. There was one rework, after the first review: the "Paid" and "Share" columns merged on a phone, and values bypassing tokens remained in the CSS. The implementer fixed it, and the second review and the checks passed. The commits were made by the implementer along the way so that they came out small; I committed the decision journal and the session recording.

What you need to do by hand. Look at the site on a phone after deployment: the system-ui font in a headless browser differs from the real one. The favicon stayed in the old green color, and I didn't touch theme-color; if they need to match the new accent, that is a separate small task. On the mobile screenshot the summary is below the first screen, because there is one column and it goes in order; if you want the summary higher, that needs a separate decision. Out of scope remained an old comment with an emoji in the bill calculation code.

The repository got 14 commits of code and documentation, a commit with the decisions on the interface style and the captions of the remove buttons, and a commit with the session recording.

Theme-color: index.html got a tag with the accent color, and a mobile browser will paint its bar in the accent. There is one color for both themes, I didn't make a separate one for the dark theme.
